comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Econometrics and Data Science degree. Current official evidence presents econometric model development, interpretation, economic causality and policy analysis as the programme’s distinctive broad identity, while Data Science is the more prediction- and automation-focused alternative. Econometrics is therefore selected as the representative route, independently of UCR fit; its first listing also supports the choice if the routes are treated as equally general.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The three options prioritise economic modelling, algorithms and AI, or finance and organisations. They differ by 45, 52.5 and 60 EC each way. Three coherent options reach the maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study derivatives, integrals and optimisation. UvA applies calculus to quantitative economics.
Both study matrix algebra, vector spaces and linear systems.
Both extend calculus to several variables. UvA also emphasises multivariate Taylor expansions and constrained optimisation.
Both study probability distributions, estimation and inference. UvA develops these topics across a longer sequence.
UvA starts with a dedicated probability course. UCR studies probability alongside statistics.
UvA continues with advanced matrix methods. UCR’s Linear Systems course focuses on signals and systems.
UvA extends the statistics sequence to asymptotic theory and properties of estimators.
Both prepare, visualise and analyse data using code.
Both teach supervised learning, including regression, classification and model validation.
Both teach programming for quantitative work. UvA integrates numerical analysis in the same course.
UvA develops a second econometrics course on issues including endogeneity, selection and censored data.
UvA has a dedicated time-series course. UCR covers some work with temporal data and prediction in other courses.
UvA requires a separate course on advanced empirical methods for individual and firm behaviour.
Both cover financial statements, investment decisions and funding. UvA also develops portfolio theory.
Both study consumer behaviour, production and markets. UvA develops these topics using mathematical optimisation.
Both study output, employment and monetary and fiscal policy using macroeconomic models.
Both study consumer choice, firm behaviour, market structure and general equilibrium. UvA gives more weight to formal models.
Both use regression and statistical inference to study economic relationships.
Both use data to investigate a research question. UCR focuses on consumer research, while UvA applies econometrics to an empirical project.
UvA introduces econometrics and actuarial science together.
UvA requires specialised study of life insurance valuation.
The example selects Risk Theory, which studies non-life insurance claims and the risk of an insurer running out of funds.
UvA continues with formal modelling of market structure and competition.
This space allows 30 EC of approved electives, a minor, study abroad or a combination with an internship.
Students develop research and presentation skills alongside the thesis project.
The research project leads to an individual thesis. UCR independent research is optional.

notes.text: UvA requires a sequence in probability, statistics and econometrics, with dedicated work in insurance mathematics, time series and microeconometrics. The UCR options combine related subjects and offer independent research as an option.

audience.programmeDescription: Econometrics and Data Science at the University of Amsterdam uses mathematics, statistics and programming to answer economic questions. This example follows the Econometrics specialisation and concludes with two linked thesis seminar courses.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines economic modelling and econometrics. The other options emphasise algorithms and AI, or financial and organisational analysis. UvA has dedicated courses in actuarial mathematics, time series and microeconometrics.
